items.title: Mississauga Road Reopens After Overnight Crash Leaves One Driver in Critical Condition
items.summary: According to Insauga, one driver was left in critical condition after a two-vehicle crash on Mississauga Road near Featherston Drive on Monday night. Peel Regional Police said both drivers were injured and taken to a local trauma centre following the collision. The crash happened at the intersection with Featherston Drive, prompting police to close Mississauga Road between Burnhamthorpe Road West and Harkiss Road. Insauga reports the road has since reopened to traffic. Police have not released further details on what caused the collision.

items.title: Tedjo Jabs at Empty Podium as Parrish Skips Latest Mississauga Mayoral Debate
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, three of Mississauga's four leading mayoral candidates faced off in a debate Monday night hosted by Policorner at City Hall, with an empty podium left for Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who chose not to attend. Bonnie Crombie, Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla took questions on stage, and Tedjo opened the debate by joking that he had seen Parrish's car in the parking lot, comparing her absence to skipping a job interview for a position she's reapplying for. The Star reports Parrish has said she committed to only three debates this campaign and prefers smaller, in-person formats like backyard groups, school gyms and church auditoriums over formal debate stages. Parrish told the Star last week that debates turn into a wrestling match verbally and don't leave enough time to properly explain her positions. She posted a video of herself speaking at a church gathering Monday night instead of attending the debate.

items.title: Incumbent Faces Office-Administration Challenger for Dufferin-Peel Catholic Board's Ward 7 Trustee Seat
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, an incumbent trustee and challenger Diana Carlesimo are the two candidates running for Mississauga's Ward 7 seat on the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board in the Oct. 26 municipal election. Carlesimo, who works in office administration, told the outlet she has lived in Ward 7 her entire life after growing up and going to school there. She said her grandparents immigrated to Mississauga from Italy in the 1950s and 1960s, and that every generation of her family has lived in the city since. Carlesimo said she has no political experience, but has volunteered at her children's school and on committees at the school board level. The Ward 7 trustee race is one of several Dufferin-Peel Catholic board contests appearing on Mississauga ballots alongside the mayoral and city council races this fall.

items.title: Voters in Toronto and Mississauga Can Begin Casting Advance Ballots as Both Mayoral Races Tighten
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, voters in both Toronto and Mississauga can begin casting ballots in advance of this month's municipal election as of Tuesday. Residents don't need photo identification to vote, but must bring a piece of ID showing their name and a Toronto or Mississauga address, depending on where they're voting. Any eligible voter can cast a ballot at any of the advance voting locations in their city, rather than being restricted to a single assigned site. CityNews reports both mayoral races are widely expected to go down to the wire. In Mississauga, incumbent Carolyn Parrish faces challenges from former mayor Bonnie Crombie and councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla. In Toronto, incumbent Olivia Chow is being challenged by Councillor Brad Bradford and former MP Chris Alexander.

items.title: Poll Finds Mississauga Voters Reject Personal Attacks in Mayoral Race, Even as Debate Clips Go Viral Online
items.summary: According to a Liaison Strategies poll reported by the Toronto Star, most Mississauga residents describe the mayoral campaign as mostly mean-spirited or a mix of respectful and mean-spirited following a heated debate last week. Three-quarters of those surveyed said personal comments or insults have no place in an election campaign, while just under a third said the race has been mostly personal attacks rather than policy debate. About 30 per cent described a mixture of personal and policy exchanges, and 17 per cent called it mostly fair political debate. The poll was conducted in the two days after the debate, which has since been widely shared online in short clips. Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin told the Star that fewer people are watching full debates but still catching the viral snippets that circulate afterward. Valentin added that voters routinely say they dislike negative campaigning even though, by his account, nothing proves more effective than negative ads.

items.title: Land Secured in Lakeview Village for Peel Police's New 600-Officer Division in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Region of Peel has finalized a land deal in Lakeview Village to build a new Peel Regional Police 14 Division in southeast Mississauga. Ward 1 Councillor Stephen Dasko announced the acquisition Monday evening, calling it a significant milestone for public safety in the growing waterfront community. The new division is expected to bring roughly 600 officers and support staff to the area, adding a substantial police presence to Ward 1 and its surroundings. Dasko said he has spent several years working with the region, Peel Regional Police and Lakeview Village representatives to get the project to this stage. The region awarded a contract for architectural consulting services back in April after issuing a request for proposals earlier in the year, and the design is now moving through its conceptual phase. A construction-industry project listing describes the planned complex as a 7,430-square-foot, two-storey police and fire facility paired with a 9,300-square-foot, three-storey parking garage. Insauga reports construction isn't expected to begin before 2028, meaning the new division is still years away from opening its doors.
